correctness.rationale: The exact L-smooth descent inequality is −h Σ g_i² sqrt(w_i)/(epsilon+sqrt(w_i))², strictly negative whenever the gradient is nonzero because w_i≥(1−beta)g_i². Compact strong-convex sublevel sets and bounded exponentially averaged squared gradients yield compact full trajectories; summable objective decrements and strict positivity force x_k→x*, then v_k→0. Full-state Lyapunov stability follows explicit strong-convexity and memory sup bounds. In scalar nonterminating quadratic trajectories q_k=(epsilon−sqrt(v_{k+1}))/(epsilon+sqrt(v_{k+1}))→1; the memory tracking ratio y_k=v_k/(a²|x_k|²) obeys an eventually contractive affine recursion, hence y_k→1. Consecutive reciprocal amplitudes differ by a quantity tending to 2a/epsilon, yielding the exact Cesàro limit k|x_k|→epsilon/(2a) and k²v_k→epsilon²/4. Exact rational finite-hit witness and replayed numerical checks corroborate, but finite checks are not the proof.

originality.rationale: The 21 October 2026 source provides the same map and a strict stability threshold but leaves the equality h=2epsilon/L outside its global-attraction and supercritical statements. The proof establishes both global attraction at that missing boundary and exact algebraic constants; neither follows by continuity from h<2epsilon/L, because the limiting linear factor is -1. The accessible related arXiv theorem statements, published semantic published-finding corpus records and related published mathematical records address strict regimes, other algorithms or period-two existence rather than the endpoint limits. Residual possibility of uninspected historical broader coverage is noted rather than excluded.
residual_risks: Not every historical proof on neutral period-doubling endpoints has been surveyed; such a theorem might subsume a special rate after additional reduction.

Independent mathematical and priority audits are not performed.

value.rationale: The source establishes subcritical attraction and supercritical cycles but its threshold does not determine the equality case. Whether an optimizer converges or bifurcates exactly at the stability frontier is a natural structural question; the global answer also refutes treating a -1 linear multiplier as loss of convergence. The exact universal k^-1 position law, k^-2 accumulator law and real finite-hit branch quantify a qualitative change from strict-regime geometric convergence and show the memory coefficient affects transients rather than leading order. The claim is not routine a priori because global descent loses its quadratic margin at equality and the memory filter is an additional state.
